rim-light-cow.summary: Edge the cow's head, fringe and sunlit side with a glowing gold rim.
rim-light-cow.tip: The sun is low on the right, so most of this gold goes on the right half of the sunlit rim: along the top of the head, the fringe, and down the cow's right side, with only a thinner glow on the cow's back edge where the after picture has it. Start each stroke on the outer edge of the shaggy coat and pull outward, so the gold hairs stick out against the hills and sky. Keep the gold to a narrow rim and leave the ginger and honey-gold locks of the shaggy coat showing, as the after picture shows.

lines.6: Press the full width of the brush on the outer edge of the coat, then turn onto its edge and lighten the pressure as you pull outward, the way the hair grows.

light-horns.summary: Run a pale cream light along the tops of both horns.
light-horns.tip: The light comes from the right and above, so the cream goes only along the top of each horn's curve, on both the horn on the left side of the head and the one on the right side of the head, as the after picture shows. Keep each stroke thin and leave the tan undersides and the dark tips showing, so the horns still end in a dark point.
paint_notes: Cream gold over the dark tan horn is see-through: paint it twice, letting the first coat dry.
